title: On the beauty of insects
content:
Abstract
Although aesthetics is recognized as a reason for the protection of biodiversity, comparatively little weight has been accorded to the grandeur of insect life beyond butterflies. Most arguments for invertebrate conservation tie to their ecosystem services, especially pollination, decomposition and nutrient cycling, and pest control. Our thesis is that more advocates for nature should be delivering messages that insect life is rich in beauty and collectively that insects have done much to enrich humanity’s existence. To bolster our argument, we review humankind’s historical relationships with insects; share some of the evolutionary and philosophical underpinnings of beauty; mention luminaries who had close associations with insects; and address the use of insects in art, textiles, and jewelry. We end with actions that would help reverse some of the negative perceptions of insects shared by many Western societies.
